answer: Each identity registers one dune grove plot, locks a 70-credit bond, and files a key-signed shade survey of tree count, spacing, and one umber dye marker. An auditor recomputes shade from the public grove shade table and checks the marker serial; shade off over 5%, a reused marker, or a double plot burns the bond. First survey 36 credits, the kth 36+6(k-1); the 1000th costs 6,030, so 1,000 fakes pay 3,033,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-canopy ring fails: one surveyor key files at most five plots per epoch. An honest agent surveys once, pays 36, and reclaims it after a clean epoch.
